content: Doing wrong is worse than suffering wrong, and escaping punishment when one has done wrong is the greatest of all evils.
author: Socrates
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

In Socrates's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
